slides.text:
A flag is optional by default. A **required** flag makes the command stop with an error when the user leaves it out, before `Run` starts.

The snippet is pseudo code, not Go.
slides.code:
app --name Ana  ->  Run starts
app             ->  error

slides.text:
Three sessions:

- **Session 1:** marking a flag as required and what it does
- **Session 2:** where a required flag applies
- **Session 3:** rules over a group of flags

A command can refuse to run until the user sets a flag. You mark a flag as required by its name, after you define it.

The call can return an error, like many calls in Go.
When a flag is missing, cobra reports it as an error and the command does not run. Your `main` still decides what the program does when `Execute` fails.

chunks.guide: A `greet` command that prints the `name` flag.
Define the flag, then mark it as required.

notes.text: Execute stops with an error if it is missing.

chunks.text:
cmd.Flags().StringVar(&name, "name", "", "who to greet")
    cmd.MarkFlagRequired("name")

exercises.title: More than one
exercises.guide: Make both the `host` and the `port` required.

chunks.guide: A `connect` command that prints a host and a port.
Each required flag gets its own call.
chunks.text:
cmd.Flags().StringVar(&host, "host", "", "server host")
    cmd.Flags().IntVar(&port, "port", 0, "server port")
    cmd.MarkFlagRequired("host")
    cmd.MarkFlagRequired("port")

exercises.title: Check the mark
exercises.guide: Mark the flag as required and handle the error of the call.

chunks.guide: A `deploy` command that prints a region.
Marking a flag returns an error. Stop the program if it fails.

notes.text: It fails when no flag has that name yet.

exercises.title: What does it print first?
exercises.guide: The program runs as `go run main.go`, with no flags. Pick the first line it prints.
exercises.explanation: Cobra checks every required flag before `Run`, and reports all the missing ones in one error, in alphabetical order. `Run` never starts.

exercises.title: What does it print?
exercises.guide: The program runs as `go run main.go`, with no flags.
exercises.explanation: A required flag must be given by the user. Its default value does not count, so the command stops before `Run`.

exercises.title: Mark the flag
exercises.guide: Fill the method that makes the `city` flag required.

slides.text: A required flag is a rule of one flag. These exercises answer three questions: what counts as set, which command checks the rule, and how flags shared by subcommands fit in.
A required flag is satisfied when the user passes it, whatever its value. A flag shared with subcommands has its own form of the mark.

exercises.title: An empty value
exercises.guide: Give a required flag an empty value and see that it still counts as set.

chunks.guide: A `deploy` command that prints the `env` between quotes.
Define the flag and require it.

notes.text: Passing --env= is enough: the rule asks if it was given, not if it has text.

chunks.text:
cmd.Flags().StringVar(&env, "env", "", "target environment")
    cmd.MarkFlagRequired("env")

exercises.title: Required on a subcommand
exercises.guide: Require a flag on a subcommand, not on the root.

chunks.guide: A root with a `build` subcommand that prints a target.
The flag belongs to `build`, so mark it there.
chunks.text:
build.Flags().StringVar(&target, "target", "", "OS to build for")
    build.MarkFlagRequired("target")

chunks.guide: Add the subcommand to the root.
chunks.text: root.AddCommand(build)

exercises.title: What does it print?
exercises.guide: The program runs as `go run main.go status`.
exercises.explanation: The requirement belongs to the `deploy` command, where the flag lives. `status` runs without it.

exercises.title: Required for every subcommand
exercises.guide: Make a flag shared by all subcommands required.

chunks.guide: A root with a `show` subcommand that prints a user.
A shared flag needs the persistent form of the mark.

notes.text: Every subcommand now needs this flag.

chunks.text:
root.AddCommand(show)
    root.PersistentFlags().StringVar(&user, "user", "", "account")
    root.MarkPersistentFlagRequired("user")

exercises.title: Share and require
exercises.guide: Fill the call that defines a flag every subcommand inherits, and the call that makes it required.

slides.text:
Sometimes the rule is about several flags at once. Cobra has three, each by the names of the flags.

The snippet is pseudo code, not Go.
slides.code:
together:   all of them or none
exclusive:  at most one of them
one-required: at least one of them

slides.text: A rule looks the flags up by name when you add it, so the flags must exist first. Rules can be combined on the same flags.

exercises.title: Flags that go together
exercises.guide: Make a certificate and its key go together.

chunks.guide: A `serve` command that prints a line.
Two flags that make a pair.
chunks.text:
cmd.Flags().String("cert", "", "TLS certificate")
    cmd.Flags().String("key", "", "TLS key")

chunks.guide: Add a rule over the pair.

notes.text: A rule over a group of flags, by name.

chunks.text: cmd.MarkFlagsRequiredTogether("cert", "key")

exercises.title: What does it print?
exercises.guide: The program runs as `go run main.go`, with no flags.
exercises.explanation: A together group is all or nothing. Giving none of the flags is fine; giving only one of them is an error.

exercises.title: Flags that exclude each other
exercises.guide: Make two output formats impossible to use together.

chunks.guide: An `export` command that prints a line.
Two switches for the output format.
chunks.text:
cmd.Flags().Bool("json", false, "as JSON")
    cmd.Flags().Bool("yaml", false, "as YAML")

chunks.guide: At most one of them can be set.
chunks.text: cmd.MarkFlagsMutuallyExclusive("json", "yaml")

exercises.title: Exactly one of two
exercises.guide: Require one source, and only one.

chunks.guide: A `fetch` command that prints a line.
Two ways to give the input.
chunks.text:
cmd.Flags().String("file", "", "read a file")
    cmd.Flags().String("url", "", "read a URL")

chunks.guide: Two rules together: at least one, and at most one.

notes.text: At least one of them must be set.

chunks.text:
cmd.MarkFlagsOneRequired("file", "url")
    cmd.MarkFlagsMutuallyExclusive("file", "url")

exercises.title: What happens?
exercises.guide: Read the order of the lines, then pick what the program does at startup.
options: It panics: the flags do not exist yet
The call creates the two flags itself
The rule is applied once the flags are defined
Execute returns an error when it runs
exercises.explanation: A group rule looks the flags up by name at the call, and panics when one is missing. Define the flags first.

exercises.title: Name the rules
exercises.guide: Fill the two rules: `cert` and `key` must be given together, and `json` and `yaml` must never be given together.
exercises.code:
package main

import "github.com/spf13/cobra"

func main() {
    cmd := &cobra.Command{Use: "export"}
    cmd.Flags().String("cert", "", "TLS cert")
    cmd.Flags().String("key", "", "TLS key")
    cmd.Flags().Bool("json", false, "as JSON")
    cmd.Flags().Bool("yaml", false, "as YAML")
    cmd.___("cert", "key")
    cmd.___("json", "yaml")
    cmd.Execute()
}
